faq: How do you know an app is unused?
We check how often it appears in your pages, its settings, what it stores and when it last did anything. If we are unsure, we ask you before taking any step.
Will removing an app delete my data?
Some apps keep data such as reviews or wishlists. We export it first and tell you what will be lost, so you can decide before anything is removed.
Can you save me money on monthly fees?
Often yes, as unused paid apps add up. We show each cost, and you decide which to cancel. We do not cancel subscriptions on your behalf without your approval.
Do you work with WordPress plugins too?
Yes. The same steps apply to WooCommerce and WordPress sites, where plugins can slow the site and leave a security risk when they are not updated.

desc:
An app and plugin review to cut cost and clutter finds the tools in your store that nobody uses, then removes or replaces them safely. Ecom Swift LLC audits every installed app and plugin, checks what depends on it and cleans up what it leaves behind.

## What is an app and plugin review?

An app and plugin review is a structured audit of every add-on installed in your store. For each one we record what it does, who uses it, what it costs and whether anything else on the store depends on it. The result is a clear keep, replace or remove decision for each item.

This is different from a general speed check or a redesign. The review looks only at the add-ons, because that is where most hidden cost and hidden risk collect.

## Why unused apps and plugins cause problems

Stores gather add-ons the way a garage gathers boxes. A review app was tried once. A pop-up tool was replaced by another pop-up tool. A freelancer installed a plugin for a one-time job. Nobody cancelled any of them.

Each leftover can load scripts on every page, keep an old subscription running and hold permission to read your customer or order data. Some leave snippets in the theme after you uninstall them, so the page still calls a service that no longer exists. When two apps do the same job, they can also fight each other and cause odd layout or checkout behavior.

## How a clean app list affects results

A smaller set of add-ons helps in three ways. Pages carry fewer scripts, so they load sooner on a phone, and faster pages keep more shoppers from leaving. Fewer overlapping tools means fewer conflicts, so features such as the cart, discounts and forms behave the same way each time. Finally, the monthly bills drop, which leaves more budget for ads, stock or better photos.

The saving is rarely a single dramatic change. It is the sum of many small ones, and the exact effect depends on which apps you remove and how heavy they were.

## What a great app review covers

- A complete inventory of installed apps, plugins and extensions, including hidden and disabled ones.
- The monthly or yearly cost of each, matched to the account that pays for it.
- The last time each tool was used and by whom.
- The data and permissions each one can access.
- Theme code, blocks and sections that each app has added.
- Overlap between tools that do the same job.
- Dependencies, such as a form that feeds an email tool.
- A written keep, replace or remove call with the reason.
- A safe removal order, so nothing breaks halfway.
- A leftover code check after each removal.

## What we do

We begin with the list. We open your admin, read the installed apps and plugins and compare them with your invoices and your theme files. Then we write a short decision sheet that shows each tool, its cost, what it touches and our recommendation.

You read the sheet and approve it. Only then do we remove anything. For each removal we note what the app changed, uninstall it, clear the leftover code and check the pages it used to affect. The Basic package covers the list and the decisions. Standard adds the removals and the code clean-up, with a speed check before and after. Premium goes deeper, merges overlapping features, sets up any replacement app and writes a short app policy your team can follow.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Cancel the subscription as well as removing the app, since removal does not always stop billing.
- Export any data you want to keep before an app is removed.
- Ask who on your team still relies on a tool before you drop it.
- Remove one app at a time and check the store between steps.
- Keep a short list of approved apps and the reason each one is there.

**Avoid:**
- Deleting apps in bulk without a test of the cart and checkout.
- Assuming that a disabled app has stopped loading code.
- Installing a new app to solve a problem a setting could solve.
- Leaving old trial apps connected to your customer data.
- Removing an app that a live form, email flow or integration still uses.

## Who this is for

This suits owners who have run a store for a year or more and feel the monthly app bill has crept up. It suits a store that took over a theme from a previous developer and does not know what is inside it. It also suits a seller who moved platforms or themes and suspects old code was left behind.

## What we need from you

Send us a list of the apps you know about and the email address on your billing accounts. We ask for access as a collaborator, staff or admin user, depending on your platform. We never need your password. For WordPress and similar stores, an administrator account created for us is enough, and you can delete it when we finish.
